headline: BWP Trust divesting former Bunnings sites and acquiring large format retail assets to enhance income growth for security holders.
reasoning: BWP Trust divested three former Bunnings sites, including one at Chadstone, where management felt the market valued the assets more than they did internally. The Chadstone asset had a shorter lease relative to the rest of the portfolio, and redevelopment risk on Bunnings vacating was a factor in the decision to sell. On the acquisition side, BWP added two large format retail assets — one in Queensland and one in Victoria — where management sees lease restructuring opportunities and income growth potential. Scatena expressed confidence in the portfolio's valuation, noting recent Bunnings-related transactions support tight yields in the sector. He highlighted strong capital flows into large format retail from both listed and unlisted REITs as supportive of current cap rates.
quote: Yeah. So typically we will look at assets all the time in terms of highest and best use, and a couple of those assets that we divested, or a number or the three assets we divested. They were former Bunnings sites and Bunnings had vacated and we had repurposed some of them in terms of retaining them. But we felt that the market perhaps valued those more than we did. Um, Chadstone being an example of an asset that we looked at. Bunnings is in that asset at the moment. It's a shorter lease relative to the other leases we have. Um, and we formed a view that, you know, the market perhaps valued that a little more than us. We look at redevelopment of that asset in the occasion, on the occasion that Bunnings would leave. But we felt divesting was in the interests of security holders. So we do that often on parts of the portfolio, and they generated very strong returns for security holders. Um, and in regards to inorganic acquisitions, yes, we're always looking at that. Very difficult to forecast. You know, we have a small team that is now dedicated to that task. And those two assets were large format retail assets, one in Queensland, one in Victoria. And those fundamentals that I mentioned before that were attracted to and also lease income growth opportunities. If we curate the lease structures there, we think there's good income growth for security holders over time.
episode_title: BWP builds on its Bunnings base

headline: Bullish on large format retail, targeting portfolio growth from current 20% weighting on favourable supply/demand fundamentals
reasoning: Scatena described a comprehensive piece of work done roughly ten months ago that identified strong structural tailwinds for large format retail including population growth, under-spacing and a shortage of floor space. The sector is adjacent to the Bunnings warehouse construct and lease structures are familiar to BWP. The trust already has 20% of its portfolio in large format retail and sees good rental income growth in those assets over time. BWP is also repurposing former Bunnings sites in South Australia and Victoria to accommodate national large format retail brands, which Scatena described as very accretive investments.
quote: We really like that market. We did a relatively comprehensive piece of work on that market probably some ten months ago. And we identified that, you know, those tailwinds that I think we've heard of in terms of population growth and under spacing and under under, well, a shortage of floor space as it relates to large format retail. You know, those fundamental drivers are positive. Um, so we like that sector. It's very adjacent to the Bunnings in terms of a warehouse construct. Um, the lease structures are what we're comfortable with. And so over time, we already have 20% of the portfolio that is essentially large format retail. And we think there is good rental income growth in those assets over time. And we would like to grow that portfolio over time. And the other thing I'd mention is that, um, we have been spending a fair bit of CapEx, uh, recently repurposing, um, assets that Bunnings vacated and we've converted those, and we're in the process of converting two of those at the moment, one in South Australia, one in Victoria, and they will profile a number of national large format retail brands. And you know that they are very accretive investments for for investors.
episode_title: BWP builds on its Bunnings base

headline: Strong capital flows into large format retail REITs support tight cap rates and underpin BWP's portfolio valuation confidence.
reasoning: Scatena noted that recent Bunnings-related market transactions support tight yields for large format retail assets. He observed meaningful capital flows into the sector from both listed and unlisted REITs seeking to grow their participation in large format retail, reflecting broad investor appetite. BWP's confidence in its own cap rates is underpinned by the quality of the underlying assets — including good ingress, egress, access, amenity, and land value — which Scatena believes will support valuations through multiple market cycles. He acknowledged the macro risk of rising interest rates but expressed comfort that asset quality provides a buffer.
quote: Look, we we we have tried to curate our portfolio to be high quality over time. And I think, you know, we do have that Bunnings covenant that is a large component of the portfolio. And we're very confident in the valuation of that portfolio. And you're seeing very recent transactions for Bunnings that that that support clearly, um, some very tight yields in regards to uh, to, to those assets, large format retail. Um, that asset class, as I said, given the income growth that sits perhaps in some of those assets, that is also quite desirable. And we've seen capital flows into LFR and other listed REITs and unlisted REIT's look to grow their participation in large format retail. So we're relatively confident that, um, you know, those cap rates reflect market. And um, but you'll call in regards to broader conditions. I think at the end of the day, we very much pride ourselves on the underlying asset quality that it has very good fundamental characteristics good ingress, good egress, good access, good amenity for the retailers and good underlying land value. And hopefully that supports the valuation, uh, through my cycles.
episode_title: BWP builds on its Bunnings base
